I read `escalation.ts`, its callers in `policy.ts` and `delegate.ts`, and the related tests. I found no crash or logic error. One design gap stands out.

**Finding (line 26, used at lines 53–54):** a `context_overflow` error marks that provider as unusable for the whole subtask, at every tier. Escalation then never tries a higher tier on that provider, even if that model has a larger context window. With a single candidate (a pinned provider, or only one configured), the ladder stops after the first overflow. It goes: dead provider → no fallback → `tierUp` finds no live provider → "escalation ladder exhausted". That contradicts the comment in `delegate.ts:304`, which says "a brief too large to start with goes up the ladder."

**Do I agree after checking?** Partly. The test at `delegate.test.ts:228` deliberately switches providers on overflow, so the switch itself is intended. But the single-provider dead end is real and untested. It only matters if a higher tier actually has a larger context window. One fix is to have `context_overflow` block only the tier that failed, not the whole provider.
